sources.title: Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025
Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 28, 2026
Lockheed Martin Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
Form 8-K: revolving credit agreements dated August 24, 2026

claims.text: Lockheed Martin designs, builds and sustains aerospace, missile, naval and space systems, principally for U.S. government agencies and allied governments.
The four reporting segments are Aeronautics, Missiles and Fire Control, Rotary and Mission Systems, and Space. Sales include products and services.

evidence.locator: Note 3, Information on Business Segments; Consolidated Statements of Earnings

claims.text: Major programs include F-35 aircraft, PAC-3 and THAAD interceptors, HIMARS launchers, Sikorsky helicopters, Aegis combat systems and Orion spacecraft.
U.S. military agencies and NASA are disclosed customers. International sales use both direct contracts and foreign military sales through the U.S. government.
The prime contractor depends on specialized suppliers, scarce materials and government funding. Supplier disruption can raise costs and delay program delivery.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Raw Materials, Suppliers and Seasonality

claims.text: Company-identified peers include Boeing, General Dynamics, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris and RTX. A peer may compete on one program and partner on another.
Interpretation: program incumbency, technical integration and sustainment capabilities support repeat work; procurement competition and government intellectual-property rights limit exclusivity.
The July results attributed missile growth to PAC-3, THAAD and Precision Strike Missile production increases. Continued growth requires successful manufacturing expansion.

evidence.locator: Segment Results, Missiles and Fire Control

claims.text: For March 30–June 28, 2026, GAAP sales were USD 20,063 million, net earnings USD 1,836 million and diluted EPS USD 7.94.

evidence.locator: Consolidated Statements of Earnings, quarter ended June 28, 2026

claims.text: Year-over-year profit comparisons benefit from the absence of large prior-year program losses. The rebound should not be treated entirely as recurring operational improvement.

evidence.locator: Consolidated Operating Profit; Net Earnings and Diluted EPS

claims.text: GAAP cash and equivalents were USD 3,791 million at June 28, 2026. GAAP operating cash inflow was USD 3,455 million for January 1–June 28, 2026.

evidence.locator: Consolidated Balance Sheets; Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows

claims.text: The July 23, 2026 results identify Jim Taiclet as chairman, president and CEO. Detailed compensation and ownership analysis remains outside this pilot.
Interpretation: evaluate cash flow and earnings after distinguishing program charges and pension adjustments. No verified current share price, multiple or fair-value estimate is included.

evidence.locator: Summary Financial Results; Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

claims.text: Monitoring trigger: subsequent results should test the higher July 2026 outlook and missile-production ramps. The next earnings announcement date was not sourced.

evidence.locator: 2026 Financial Outlook; Missiles and Fire Control

claims.text: Concentrated exposure to F-35, complex fixed-price development and supplier performance can produce delays or losses. Repeat material program charges would weaken an execution-improvement thesis.
Interpretation: upside requires profitable backlog conversion; downside includes program overruns or delayed funding. Test margin quality and working-capital needs before extrapolating the quarter.
RTX is both a named competitor and Lockheed Martin’s Javelin joint-venture partner. The Javelin relationship is specific; it does not imply cooperation across all programs.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Missiles and Fire Control / Javelin; Competition

claims.text: On August 24, 2026, Lockheed Martin entered a replacement revolving credit agreement and extended another facility. The related filing reports no borrowing at the new facility’s closing.

evidence.locator: Item 1.01, 364-Day Revolving Credit Agreement; Extension of 5-Year Revolving Credit Agreement

gaps: No current stock price, consensus estimates or valuation multiples were sourced.
Filings-first pilot, with latest reported results through June 28, 2026; not an exhaustive subsequent news or contract-award feed.
Full debt maturities, pensions, compensation incentives and pending transaction developments require deeper review.
No independently verified next earnings release date.
